html:
The Southeastern Pomo lived around East Lake and Lower Lake, the eastern arms of Clear Lake in Lake County, northern California. They spoke one of the seven Pomoan languages, also known by the names of its communities: Elem, Koi and Sulfur Bank Pomo.

Their villages stood on islands and lakeshores. They fished, gathered tule and acorns, and traded with the Wappo and Patwin. Ranchers took over the Clear Lake basin in the 1840s, and in 1850 US soldiers killed many Pomo at the lake in the Bloody Island massacre. Later the Sulphur Bank mercury mine was dug beside the Elem community, poisoning land and lake. The Elem Indian Colony and the Koi Nation carry the people on today, though the language has almost no speakers left.
